a: The sun: the blazing star that supplies the earth with light and heat.
‘Ad-duha’: the time when the sun has risen high and the day has grown strong.
The moon: a moving body that revolves around the earth and illuminates it at night.
An adverb that indicates, in most cases, future time.
Day: the time from sunrise to sunset.
An adverb that indicates, in most cases, future time.
That is, it displayed the sun to whoever sees; or it cleared away the night, that is, removed its darkness by the day.
Night: the time from sunset to sunrise.
An adverb that indicates, in most cases, future time.
It covers it when the sun sets and the horizons grow dark.
‘As-sama’: what is meant is the sky, the celestial body.
‘Ma’: it may be relative or verbal-noun (masdariyya).
The building of the sky: its raising, establishing, and creating it firmly made.
The well-known planet on whose surface we live, or a part of it.
‘Ma’: it may be relative or verbal-noun (masdariyya).
Nafs: the self, that is, the spirit and the body together.
‘Ma’: it may be relative or verbal-noun (masdariyya).
Allah perfected its creation for performing its task.
And He cast into its mind and made clear to it.
Its sins and its disbelief; what is meant is the path of evil.
Taqwa: guarding oneself and making a shield from Allah’s punishment by following His commands and avoiding His prohibitions; what is meant is the path of good.
A relative noun in the meaning of ‘alladhi’ (who), specific to rational beings.
He purified it and made it grow with good.
He lost and did not attain what he sought.
A relative noun in the meaning of ‘alladhi’ (who), specific to rational beings.
He concealed its virtues and drove it to wickedness; or he hid himself in sins.

An Arab people that perished before the appearance of Islam; named after one of the grandsons of Nuh, or so named because of the scarcity of water among them — it is said: ‘thamada al-ma’’, the water became scant; their prophet was Salih.
Because of its tyranny, its aggression, its exceeding the limit, and its excess in disobedience.
An adverb that indicates, in most cases, past time.
He rose up and rushed to hamstring the she-camel.
The most miserable of it in condition.
Lam: a preposition conveying the meaning of conveying (informing).
The messenger: the bearer of the divine message, whether a human prophet or an angel among the angels; the messenger here is Salih, peace be upon him.

A name of the Most High Essence, unique in divinity, whose existence is necessary, worshipped by right; it is the Word of Majesty (lafz al-jalalah) comprehending the meanings of all of Allah’s perfect attributes.

‘The she-camel of Allah’: attributed to Allah, glorified is He, to honour her and to warn them; the naqah is the female of camels; what is meant is the she-camel of Salih, peace be upon him, which Allah created from a rock, not from two parents.

A name of the Most High Essence, unique in divinity, whose existence is necessary, worshipped by right; it is the Word of Majesty (lafz al-jalalah) comprehending the meanings of all of Allah’s perfect attributes.

‘Suqyaha’: suqya is a noun from ‘saqy’ (giving drink); the expression ‘the she-camel of Allah and her drink’ conveys a warning against preventing the she-camel from drinking, and a command to protect her and her drink.
And they attributed lying to him, or did not believe in him.
‘Damdama ‘alayhim’: He crushed them and destroyed them after He became angry with them.
‘ʿAlā’: a preposition used to affirm bounty.
Sin: transgression, and the forbidden among acts.
‘Fa-sawwaha’: He made the destruction upon them equal (for all).
‘Wa la yakhafu’: and He does not dread.
The consequence of what He did to them, or the outcome of this punishment.
